An angle ends at a point on the unit circle. Its quadrant determines the signs of x and y.
Cosine is the horizontal x-coordinate on the unit circle.
Find the reference angle, identify the quadrant, and use the sign of x.
At 0°, the point is (1,0), so cosine is 1.
At 180°, the point is (−1,0), so cosine is −1.
120° is in Quadrant II with reference angle 60°.
225° is in Quadrant III with reference angle 45°.
A unit-circle point is in Quadrant IV with y=−3/5.
x²=1−9/25=16/25; x=+4/5 because Quadrant IV has positive x.
